Test run (python -m pytest): test_plain PASS, test_total PASS, test_half_cent_rounds_up FAIL (assert 959 == 960).

Why test_half_cent_rounds_up fails:
- cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
- int() cuts off the fraction. It does not round.
- 5% off 1010 is 959.5. int(959.5) gives 959. The test expects 960.
- test_total passes only by luck: 10% off 399 is 359.1, and cutting and rounding both give 359.
- This matches the open TODO item: "fix rounding in cart.total (customers see totals one cent short)".

What a fix would need (not done, you asked a question):
- Round half up in whole cents. Python's round() rounds half to even (round(959.5) is 960, but round(958.5) is 958), so it is not a safe half-up rule.
- Float math can also land just under .5. Integer math avoids both: compute in cents times 100, then add 50 and floor divide by 100.

I changed no code. Tell me if you want the fix made before tonight.
